text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Greek President Costis Stephanopoulos hold talks in Cairo. They stress the need for a just and complete peace in the Middle East region based on the land for peace principle.
Stephanopoulos says Greece will lobby the Palestinian cause among the other European Union members.

- Egyptian delegation in Saudi Arabia says there are discussions between the two countries to set up a joint free zone and increase bilateral trade, as well as increase activities and investment of businessmen in both countries.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and U.S. Ambassador to Egypt Edward Walker discuss the Middle East peace process and the difficulties still in its way, as well as the visit to the region of U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross. U.S. Congress members are to visit Egypt in January.
- Arab contacts are underway for a meeting in the United Nations to discuss a resolution asking Israel to stop settlements expansion.
- Mubarak says that the building of settlements is the biggest possible "bomb" to disrupt the peace process.
